body:
Rebased onto current `main` (v2.0.1) and addressed the review — this is ready for another look.

### Resync
Rebased the two scheme commits onto `upstream/main` (was based on a pre-2.0.0 commit, ~124 behind). The only conflict was the v2.0.0 modular refactor moving `decimal_u256` to `x402_types::util`; resolved by taking it from there and keeping the scheme's `decimal_u128` from `chain::types`. Branch is now `main` + 3 commits, fast-forward-clean (0 behind), so the CONFLICTING state should clear.

### Review note — viem parity (thanks @Adelagric)
Added your two cross-implementation golden vectors to `tests/batch_settlement_parity.rs`:
- `channel_id_matches_viem_reference_vector` → `0x5fafb915…fb28bd`
- `voucher_digest_matches_viem_reference_vector` → `0xa2874adb…fa2246`

Both **pass**, so `alloy_sol_types`' typed-data hashing is now pinned byte-for-byte against viem (and your hand-rolled keccak256+abi.encode path) — a drift in any type string, the domain, or the struct encoding now fails here instead of silently rejecting real client signatures. The wider suite you mentioned (signature recovery, full `verify_voucher` round-trip, claim/settle wire-shape) would be very welcome as a follow-up PR against this branch.

### #92 coverage
- `v2-eip155-batch-settlement` facilitator handler (`X402SchemeFacilitator`: verify/settle/supported) in `x402-chain-eip155`, registered via `SchemeBlueprints` ✅
- EIP-712 vectors as conformance tests ✅ (the two above)
- Honest scope, matching #92: this is the facilitator core + voucher verification + server-authored claim/settle. The channel-lifecycle long-tail (cooperative refund, recovery-after-state-loss, withdrawal monitoring, multi-policy claim) and the client side (`X402SchemeClient`/`PaymentCandidate`) are **not** in this PR — follow-ups.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p x402-chain-eip155 --features facilitator` → **9/9** parity + 83 unit + 3 integration green
- `cargo build --workspace` clean on v2.0.1
- Live smoke: facilitator boots on Base Sepolia and `GET /supported` advertises `eip155:84532 → batch-settlement v2` alongside `exact`/`upto`

@Adelagric — would appreciate your review / merge when you have a moment. Happy to fold in the extended parity vectors here or take them as your follow-up, whichever you prefer.

Reviewed from the parity / conformance side — the surface I've independently implemented and cross-tested against viem, not the full provider/RPC plumbing, so scope my read accordingly.

**EIP-712 + voucher crypto:** solid. The two viem-anchored vectors now on the branch pin `alloy_sol_types`' typed-data derivation against viem byte-for-byte — a drift in any type string, domain field, or struct encoding fails the suite here instead of silently rejecting real client signatures. I pushed the wider suite you asked for as #1 against this branch (signature recovery, full `verify_voucher` round-trip, claim/settle wire-shape) — 17/17 green, fold it in whenever suits.

**Scope:** the boundary matches #92 cleanly — facilitator core + voucher verification + server-authored claim/settle in; the channel-lifecycle long-tail (cooperative refund, recovery-after-state-loss, withdrawal monitoring, multi-policy claim) + the client side out. Worth flagging for reviewers: that excluded long-tail is exactly the failure surface being worked upstream as the "Two-Phase Gap" (x402-foundation/x402#2294), so deferring it here is the right call rather than a gap — it lines up with where the recovery semantics are still being settled at the spec level.

One thing I can't vouch for from here: the on-chain `verify`/`settle` provider path against a live facilitator — that needs an integration run, which your `GET /supported` smoke test only partially covers. From the conformance/parity angle this looks ready; the merge call is the x402-rs maintainers'.

Thanks @Adelagric — folded your full suite in. Since the rebase onto upstream v2.0.1 diverged the base (your #1 was opened against the pre-rebase branch), a clean merge of #1 wasn't possible, so I adopted your `batch_settlement_parity.rs` directly on `feature/batch-settlement-port` with a `Co-authored-by` credit (commit `b2a75cd`) and closed #1 in its favor. **17/17 green on v2.0.1** — channelId + voucher-digest golden vectors (incl. nonzero-salt, chain-id-1, u128::MAX, zero), signature recovery, full `verify_voucher` round-trip, and claim/settle wire-shape.

Good call on the **Two-Phase Gap** (x402-foundation/x402#2294) — agreed that deferring cooperative refund / recovery-after-state-loss / withdrawal monitoring here is correct while those recovery semantics settle at the spec level, not a gap in this PR.

On the one thing you (rightly) couldn't vouch for — the **on-chain `verify`/`settle` path against a live facilitator**: that integration run is queued. We're publishing a `:beta` facilitator image (this scheme on v2.0.1 + a prometheus overlay) and will run deposit → cumulative voucher → verify+settle against it + the live Base-Sepolia contracts (`x402BatchSettlement`/deposit collectors are deployed). I'll post that integration result here so the on-chain leg is covered beyond the `/supported` smoke. Merge call is the maintainers'.

Thanks @bussyjd — the adoption and the co-author credit are both appreciated, and closing #1 in favor of the folded suite is the right call given the base divergence.

The queued integration run is the right next step: the live deposit → cumulative voucher → verify+settle against the deployed `x402BatchSettlement` contracts is exactly what closes the on-chain leg I couldn't vouch for from the parity side. One thing that might save you a debugging cycle when you run the live settle leg — I hit two facilitator ordering races doing the same flow single-process: the `claim`/`settle` nonce collision (`replacement transaction underpriced`) and the post-claim indexer lag (`nothing_to_settle`). Both are written up with on-chain tx hashes in x402-foundation/x402#2471, and the closed-loop runs (settledAmount matching the on-chain recipient delta to the raw unit) are in Adelagric/x402-batch-settlement if useful to compare against.

Nice work on the scheme port.
